messages.subject: Re: Following adaptation for sampler other than RW
messages.subject_clean: Following adaptation for sampler other than RW
messages.body_plain:
To answer your questions:

1. At present, when you specify adaptive=FALSE (thereby using a fixed proposal scale), the RW sampler doesn't record when / how often / the proportion of transitions (the acceptance rate).  And I'm hesitant to slow it down by tracking this, when it's non-adaptive.  That said, you could easily grab the code form GitHub
https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/blob/devel/packages/nimble/R/MCMC_samplers.R#L165
And modify it so that it still tracks this information even when adaptive=FALSE, but merely doesn't change the scale.  This could be done as easily as removing the one line:
scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
I'll put this modified code, below, and you would only have to remove the RW samplers that are assigned, and add (using conf$addSampler) the new "RW2" sampler, defined below.  To use this sampler, you would need to leave the default of adaptive=TRUE, and also set this nimble system option nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE).

Another option would be for you to use the posterior samples calculate the RW acceptance rate, based on the proportion of times it successfully transitions (e.g., the parameter changes value).

2. About the target acceptance rate, right now it's hard-coded into the RW sampler at 0.44.  You can also change this in the code below, if you wish.  Or, if it's useful to you, I'm happy to change this into a (user-modifiable) "control list argument", with default value 0.44.  It would be a straightforward change to make, and could go into our next upcoming release (in a couple weeks).  Let me know if that sounds helpful.

Cheers,
Daniel

sampler_RW2 <- nimbleFunction(
    name = 'sampler_RW2',
    contains = sampler_BASE,
    setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
        ## control list extraction
        logScale            <- if(!is.null(control$log))                 control$log                 else FALSE
        reflective          <- if(!is.null(control$reflective))          control$reflective          else FALSE
        adaptive            <- if(!is.null(control$adaptive))            control$adaptive            else TRUE
        adaptInterval       <- if(!is.null(control$adaptInterval))       control$adaptInterval       else 200
        adaptFactorExponent <- if(!is.null(control$adaptFactorExponent)) control$adaptFactorExponent else 0.8
        scale               <- if(!is.null(control$scale))               control$scale               else 1
        ## node list generation
        targetAsScalar <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
        calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
        calcNodesNoSelf <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE)
        isStochCalcNodesNoSelf <- model$isStoch(calcNodesNoSelf)   ## should be made faster
        calcNodesNoSelfDeterm <- calcNodesNoSelf[!isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
        calcNodesNoSelfStoch <- calcNodesNoSelf[isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
        ## numeric value generation
        scaleOriginal <- scale
        timesRan      <- 0
        timesAccepted <- 0
        timesAdapted  <- 0
        scaleHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
        acceptanceHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
        if(nimbleOptions('MCMCsaveHistory')) {
            saveMCMChistory <- TRUE
        } else saveMCMChistory <- FALSE
        optimalAR     <- 0.44
        gamma1        <- 0
        ## checks
        if(length(targetAsScalar) > 1)   stop('cannot use RW sampler on more than one target; try RW_block sampler')
        if(model$isDiscrete(target))     stop('cannot use RW sampler on discrete-valued target; try slice sampler')
        if(logScale & reflective)        stop('cannot use reflective RW sampler on a log scale (i.e. with options log=TRUE and reflective=TRUE')
        if(adaptFactorExponent < 0)      stop('cannot use RW sampler with adaptFactorExponent control parameter less than 0')
        if(scale < 0)                    stop('cannot use RW sampler with scale control parameter less than 0')
    },
    run = function() {
        currentValue <- model[[target]]
        propLogScale <- 0
        if(logScale) { propLogScale <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = scale)
                       propValue <- currentValue * exp(propLogScale)
        } else         propValue <- rnorm(1, mean = currentValue,  sd = scale)
        if(reflective) {
            lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
            upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
            while(propValue < lower | propValue > upper) {
                if(propValue < lower) propValue <- 2*lower - propValue
                if(propValue > upper) propValue <- 2*upper - propValue
            }
        }
        model[[target]] <<- propValue
        logMHR <- calculateDiff(model, target)
        if(logMHR == -Inf) {
            nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
            ## Drawing a random number is needed during first testing
            ## of this step in order to keep the random numbers identical
            ## to old behavior to see if tests that depend on particular
            ## sample sequences pass.  Rather than calling runif(1, 0, 1) here,
            ## we call decide() to ensure same behavior.
            ## jump <- decide(logMHR)
            ## When new behavior is acceptable, we can remove the above line
            ## and uncomment the following:
            jump <- FALSE
        } else {
            logMHR <- logMHR + calculateDiff(model, calcNodesNoSelf) + propLogScale
            jump <- decide(logMHR)
            if(jump) {
                nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
                nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
                nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
            } else {
                nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
                nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
                nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
            }
        }
        if(adaptive)     adaptiveProcedure(jump)
    },
    methods = list(
        adaptiveProcedure = function(jump = logical()) {
            timesRan <<- timesRan + 1
            if(jump)     timesAccepted <<- timesAccepted + 1
            if(timesRan %% adaptInterval == 0) {
                acceptanceRate <- timesAccepted / timesRan
                timesAdapted <<- timesAdapted + 1
                if(saveMCMChistory) {
                    setSize(scaleHistory, timesAdapted)                 ## scaleHistory
                    scaleHistory[timesAdapted] <<- scale                ## scaleHistory
                    setSize(acceptanceHistory, timesAdapted)            ## scaleHistory
                    acceptanceHistory[timesAdapted] <<- acceptanceRate  ## scaleHistory
                }
                gamma1 <<- 1/((timesAdapted + 3)^adaptFactorExponent)
                gamma2 <- 10 * gamma1
                adaptFactor <- exp(gamma2 * (acceptanceRate - optimalAR))
                ######scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
                ## If there are upper and lower bounds, enforce a maximum scale of
                ## 0.5 * (upper-lower).  This is arbitrary but reasonable.
                ## Otherwise, for a poorly-informed posterior,
                ## the scale could grow without bound to try to reduce
                ## acceptance probability.  This creates enormous cost of
                ## reflections.
                if(reflective) {
                    lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
                    upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
                    if(scale >= 0.5*(upper-lower)) {
                        scale <<- 0.5*(upper-lower)
                    }
                }
                timesRan <<- 0
                timesAccepted <<- 0
            }
        },
        getScaleHistory = function() {       ## scaleHistory
            returnType(double(1))
            if(saveMCMChistory) {
                return(scaleHistory)
            } else {
                print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
                return(numeric(1, 0))
            }
        },
        getAcceptanceHistory = function() {  ## scaleHistory
            returnType(double(1))
            if(saveMCMChistory) {
                return(acceptanceHistory)
            } else {
                print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
                return(numeric(1, 0))
            }
        },
        ##getScaleHistoryExpanded = function() {                                                 ## scaleHistory
        ##    scaleHistoryExpanded <- numeric(timesAdapted*adaptInterval, init=FALSE)            ## scaleHistory
        ##    for(iTA in 1:timesAdapted)                                                         ## scaleHistory
        ##        for(j in 1:adaptInterval)                                                      ## scaleHistory
        ##            scaleHistoryExpanded[(iTA-1)*adaptInterval+j] <- scaleHistory[iTA]         ## scaleHistory
        ##    returnType(double(1)); return(scaleHistoryExpanded) },                             ## scaleHistory
        reset = function() {
            scale <<- scaleOriginal
            timesRan      <<- 0
            timesAccepted <<- 0
            timesAdapted  <<- 0
            if(saveMCMChistory) {
                scaleHistory  <<- c(0, 0)    ## scaleHistory
                acceptanceHistory  <<- c(0, 0)
            }
            gamma1 <<- 0
        }
    )
)

So I wanted to try other samplers (currently the slice) to see if it could ease the process and I was curious to see if there was a similar process during the adapatation phase for the slice samplers (but maybe you would have other suggestions for such cases).
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Thanks in advance,

messages.body_plain:
Thanks a lot for the answer, that helps a lot.

1. Thank you, I will look into that to test it. Indeed that may be a niche issue to track acceptance without adaptation so I totally understand the choice.
I always thought that the model kept proposing a new sample until it was accepted before updating the other node so that's a great thing to know it is not the case! Thanks for highlighting the possibility to look into the posterior, I won't use it because I use thinning but that's good to know for the future.

2. Thanks for pointing me that idea, I will definitely want to try that.

3. If I understood correctly, at each iteration all nodes are updated but for some of them (56% based on the targeted 0.44 acceptance rate) the value stays the same because the proposal is refused. Is it possible to force more update on one node while other nodes are updated less frequently ? e.g. if node A is highly autocorrelated and have a poor mixing while node B has a good mixing, I would want node A to have a lower acceptance of proposal (therefore less autocorrelated) but to update until one proposal is accepted, before updating node B, so it would spare unneeded calculations on the update of node B, before node A finds a good proposal.

Cheers,
Rémi

Le 13/08/2020 à 19:07, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> To answer your questions:
>
> 1. At present, when you specify adaptive=FALSE (thereby using a fixed proposal scale), the RW sampler doesn't record when / how often / the proportion of transitions (the acceptance rate).  And I'm hesitant to slow it down by tracking this, when it's non-adaptive.  That said, you could easily grab the code form GitHub
> https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/blob/devel/packages/nimble/R/MCMC_samplers.R#L165
> And modify it so that it still tracks this information even when adaptive=FALSE, but merely doesn't change the scale.  This could be done as easily as removing the one line:
> scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> I'll put this modified code, below, and you would only have to remove the RW samplers that are assigned, and add (using conf$addSampler) the new "RW2" sampler, defined below.  To use this sampler, you would need to leave the default of adaptive=TRUE, and also set this nimble system option nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE).
>
> Another option would be for you to use the posterior samples calculate the RW acceptance rate, based on the proportion of times it successfully transitions (e.g., the parameter changes value).
>
> 2. About the target acceptance rate, right now it's hard-coded into the RW sampler at 0.44.  You can also change this in the code below, if you wish.  Or, if it's useful to you, I'm happy to change this into a (user-modifiable) "control list argument", with default value 0.44.  It would be a straightforward change to make, and could go into our next upcoming release (in a couple weeks).  Let me know if that sounds helpful.
>
> Cheers,
> Daniel
>
>
>
> sampler_RW2 <- nimbleFunction(
>     name = 'sampler_RW2',
>     contains = sampler_BASE,
>     setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
>         ## control list extraction
>         logScale            <- if(!is.null(control$log))                 control$log                 else FALSE
>         reflective          <- if(!is.null(control$reflective))          control$reflective          else FALSE
>         adaptive            <- if(!is.null(control$adaptive))            control$adaptive            else TRUE
>         adaptInterval       <- if(!is.null(control$adaptInterval))       control$adaptInterval       else 200
>         adaptFactorExponent <- if(!is.null(control$adaptFactorExponent)) control$adaptFactorExponent else 0.8
>         scale               <- if(!is.null(control$scale))               control$scale               else 1
>         ## node list generation
>         targetAsScalar <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
>         calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
>         calcNodesNoSelf <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE)
>         isStochCalcNodesNoSelf <- model$isStoch(calcNodesNoSelf)   ## should be made faster
>         calcNodesNoSelfDeterm <- calcNodesNoSelf[!isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
>         calcNodesNoSelfStoch <- calcNodesNoSelf[isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
>         ## numeric value generation
>         scaleOriginal <- scale
>         timesRan      <- 0
>         timesAccepted <- 0
>         timesAdapted  <- 0
>         scaleHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
>         acceptanceHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
>         if(nimbleOptions('MCMCsaveHistory')) {
>             saveMCMChistory <- TRUE
>         } else saveMCMChistory <- FALSE
>         optimalAR     <- 0.44
>         gamma1        <- 0
>         ## checks
>         if(length(targetAsScalar) > 1)   stop('cannot use RW sampler on more than one target; try RW_block sampler')
>         if(model$isDiscrete(target))     stop('cannot use RW sampler on discrete-valued target; try slice sampler')
>         if(logScale & reflective)        stop('cannot use reflective RW sampler on a log scale (i.e. with options log=TRUE and reflective=TRUE')
>         if(adaptFactorExponent < 0)      stop('cannot use RW sampler with adaptFactorExponent control parameter less than 0')
>         if(scale < 0)                    stop('cannot use RW sampler with scale control parameter less than 0')
>     },
>     run = function() {
>         currentValue <- model[[target]]
>         propLogScale <- 0
>         if(logScale) { propLogScale <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = scale)
>                        propValue <- currentValue * exp(propLogScale)
>         } else         propValue <- rnorm(1, mean = currentValue,  sd = scale)
>         if(reflective) {
>             lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
>             upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
>             while(propValue < lower | propValue > upper) {
>                 if(propValue < lower) propValue <- 2*lower - propValue
>                 if(propValue > upper) propValue <- 2*upper - propValue
>             }
>         }
>         model[[target]] <<- propValue
>         logMHR <- calculateDiff(model, target)
>         if(logMHR == -Inf) {
>             nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
>             ## Drawing a random number is needed during first testing
>             ## of this step in order to keep the random numbers identical
>             ## to old behavior to see if tests that depend on particular
>             ## sample sequences pass.  Rather than calling runif(1, 0, 1) here,
>             ## we call decide() to ensure same behavior.
>             ## jump <- decide(logMHR)
>             ## When new behavior is acceptable, we can remove the above line
>             ## and uncomment the following:
>             jump <- FALSE
>         } else {
>             logMHR <- logMHR + calculateDiff(model, calcNodesNoSelf) + propLogScale
>             jump <- decide(logMHR)
>             if(jump) {
>                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
>                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
>                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
>             } else {
>                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
>                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
>                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
>             }
>         }
>         if(adaptive)     adaptiveProcedure(jump)
>     },
>     methods = list(
>         adaptiveProcedure = function(jump = logical()) {
>             timesRan <<- timesRan + 1
>             if(jump)     timesAccepted <<- timesAccepted + 1
>             if(timesRan %% adaptInterval == 0) {
>                 acceptanceRate <- timesAccepted / timesRan
>                 timesAdapted <<- timesAdapted + 1
>                 if(saveMCMChistory) {
>                     setSize(scaleHistory, timesAdapted)                 ## scaleHistory
>                     scaleHistory[timesAdapted] <<- scale                ## scaleHistory
>                     setSize(acceptanceHistory, timesAdapted)            ## scaleHistory
>                     acceptanceHistory[timesAdapted] <<- acceptanceRate  ## scaleHistory
>                 }
>                 gamma1 <<- 1/((timesAdapted + 3)^adaptFactorExponent)
>                 gamma2 <- 10 * gamma1
>                 adaptFactor <- exp(gamma2 * (acceptanceRate - optimalAR))
>                 ######scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
>                 ## If there are upper and lower bounds, enforce a maximum scale of
>                 ## 0.5 * (upper-lower).  This is arbitrary but reasonable.
>                 ## Otherwise, for a poorly-informed posterior,
>                 ## the scale could grow without bound to try to reduce
>                 ## acceptance probability.  This creates enormous cost of
>                 ## reflections.
>                 if(reflective) {
>                     lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
>                     upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
>                     if(scale >= 0.5*(upper-lower)) {
>                         scale <<- 0.5*(upper-lower)
>                     }
>                 }
>                 timesRan <<- 0
>                 timesAccepted <<- 0
>             }
>         },
>         getScaleHistory = function() {       ## scaleHistory
>             returnType(double(1))
>             if(saveMCMChistory) {
>                 return(scaleHistory)
>             } else {
>                 print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
>                 return(numeric(1, 0))
>             }
>         },
>         getAcceptanceHistory = function() {  ## scaleHistory
>             returnType(double(1))
>             if(saveMCMChistory) {
>                 return(acceptanceHistory)
>             } else {
>                 print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
>                 return(numeric(1, 0))
>             }
>         },
>         ##getScaleHistoryExpanded = function() {                                                 ## scaleHistory
>         ##    scaleHistoryExpanded <- numeric(timesAdapted*adaptInterval, init=FALSE)            ## scaleHistory
>         ##    for(iTA in 1:timesAdapted)                                                         ## scaleHistory
>         ##        for(j in 1:adaptInterval)                                                      ## scaleHistory
>         ##            scaleHistoryExpanded[(iTA-1)*adaptInterval+j] <- scaleHistory[iTA]         ## scaleHistory
>         ##    returnType(double(1)); return(scaleHistoryExpanded) },                             ## scaleHistory
>         reset = function() {
>             scale <<- scaleOriginal
>             timesRan      <<- 0
>             timesAccepted <<- 0
>             timesAdapted  <<- 0
>             if(saveMCMChistory) {
>                 scaleHistory  <<- c(0, 0)    ## scaleHistory
>                 acceptanceHistory  <<- c(0, 0)
>             }
>             gamma1 <<- 0
>         }
>     )
> )
>
>
>

> On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 12:56 PM Rémi Patin <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > I meant tracking the history of the acceptance rate of the sampler. Which from what I understood is still meaningful without adaptation for a sampler. Although it may be relatively constant, I would be interested by its level.
> >
> > However, I am also interested if you can make the RW sampler to tune itself towards another acceptance rate (right now it tunes toward something like 0.4 if I'm not mistaken)
> >
> > Le 13/08/2020 à 18:40, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> > > Thanks for following up, Rémi.   One question, when you say "would be possible to use non-adaptive RW and still follow acceptance rate?", by the phrase "follow the acceptance rate", do you mean that the RW sampler itself tunes itself towards some "optimal" acceptance rate?  Or, do you mean for you to track (follow) the history of the acceptance rate of the sampler?
> > >
> > > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 10:40 AM remi....@gmail.com <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Hi All,
> > > > Just a quick follow-up on the different solution I tested following Perry and Daniel advices:
> > > >
> > > > - For following the adaptation phase of the slice sampler, I tested the manual solution of stopping the mcmc every 200 runs but it is quite time consuming to run through numerous samplers each time to get the `width` (it is still running in fact). I may test at some point the implementation I proposed in the dev version of nimble, but did not have time for it yet.
> > > >
> > > > - I also did some test by fixing the scale of the different RW samplers involved in the problematic nodes. Nothing conclusive for now. But I was wondering if it would be possible to use non-adaptive RW and still follow acceptance rate  ?
> > > >
> > > > Best,
> > > > Rémi
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Friday, July 31, 2020 at 5:04:21 PM UTC+2 pdevalpine wrote:
> > > > > Hi Rémi,
> > > > >
> > > > > Sure that makes sense.  You could write a for loop to iterate over samplers for many nodes to set the proposal scale and turn the adapt flag FALSE for each one.  I suggested it because it sounded like you were conjecturing that the adaptation has not resulted in proposal scales that you think are most efficient.  (We usually think of efficiency in terms of (effective sample size) / computation time.  The computation time shouldn't change much or at all for different proposal scales, but the effective sample sizes almost certainly will.)  That is possible.  If you increase proposal scale, it may or may not increase effective sample size.  If it does, then fewer iterations would be needed.  I hope that helps.  Let us know if you get interesting results.
> > > > >
> > > > > -Perry
> > > > >
> > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 7:48 AM Rémi PATIN <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > Hi Perry,
> > > > > > Thank you for the suggestion and the explanations to do it, I will give it a try. I am however a bit afraid to fix the RW proposal scale, because it concerns around ~2000 nodes. So I am not sure whether a single (or even a few) scale for all the nodes could do the trick.
> > > > > > I suppose if I manually fix the scale to higher value than produced by the adaptation phase, acceptation rate for those nodes will drop leading to slower iteration through those nodes. Meanwhile the samples should be less autocorrelated and less iterations would be needed ?
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Concerning initial values, the model should have relatively good ones for most nodes. I know they have already worked on that and I think that we are currently using older model outputs to initiate the nodes in question. But I will keep that in mind, this could still be problematic.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > Rémi
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Le vendredi 31 juillet 2020 16:18:06 UTC+2, pdevalpine a écrit :
> > > > > > > Hi Rémi,
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > If you think the RW proposal scale has adapted to a value that is too small, I can give three suggestions for exploring the issue.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 1. At the stage of the MCMC configuration (after configureMCMC) but before building the MCMC (before buildMCMC), find the relevant sampler by inspection of mcmcConf$printSamplers() or mcmcConf$getSamplers().  (Here mcmcConf is the object returned by configureMCMC).  Then modify the control list of that sampler to have adapt=FALSE and scale=<your choice>.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 2. You can make the same settings by modifying the MCMC (after buildMCMC).  If you do it in the uncompiled version (before compileNimble), you can modify mcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$scale and mcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$adapt, where mcmc is the uncompiled MCMC.  Those values will then be copied to the compiled version to initialize it during compileNimble.  If you want to do it after compileNimble (with say Cmcmc instead of mcmc, where Cmcmc is the compiled version), you will need the same nimbleOptions setting Daniel provided.  You may want to do it this way because you could run it for a while, look at the scale value, then manually adjust it and continue running (with reset = FALSE) to experiment.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 3. Sometimes providing good initial values can improve the outcome of the RW adaptation.  If the initial values are far from the main posterior region, then much of the adaptation can occur during updates that are just finding the main posterior region, which can behave very differently that updates in the main region.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > HTH
> > > > > > > -Perry
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 6:51 AM Daniel Turek <db...@williams.edu> wrote:
> > > > > > > > Good question, Rémi.  And I'm glad to hear you found the diagnostic information (scaleHistory, acceptanceRateHistory, etc) in the RW sampler to be helpful.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > At present, there's no such facilities in the slice sampler to record this history of the adaption process.  The slice sampler does adapt (every adaptInterval MCMC iterations), to modify the internal "width" variable, to make this "extension" width of the horizontal slice more suitable for the scale of the posterior distribution.  So, yes, tracking this "widthHistory" would be analogous to the adaptation history information in the RW sampler.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > At present, this information is not tracked in the slice sampler, but similar methods "getWidthHistory" could be added to the slice sampler.  I don't believe there are plans for adding it at the moment, but we would certainly welcome (and review) a pull-request to add this to the system.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Short of that, modifying the sampler code and/or the nimble code base, you could also track this "width history" by extracting the "width" variable from the slice sampler after each MCMC iteration, making sure to set the nimble option:
> > > > > > > > nimbleOptions(buildInterfacesForCompiledNestedNimbleFunctions = TRUE)

> > > > > > > > This would work fine, and accomplish your goals.  A short example showing how to do that is below.

> > > > > > > > })

> > > > > > > > inits <- list(a = 0)
> > > > > > > >

> > > > > > > > Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
> > > > > > > > Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > niter <- 10000
> > > > > > > > set.seed(0)
> > > > > > > > widthHistory <- numeric(niter)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > for(i in 1:niter) {
> > > > > > > >     Cmcmc$run(1, reset = (i==1))
> > > > > > > >     widthHistory[i] <- Cmcmc$samplerFunctions[[1]]$width
> > > > > > > > }
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > samples <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > plot(1:niter, widthHistory, type = 'l')
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 2:27 AM Rémi PATIN <remi...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > Hi all,
> > > > > > > > > I have seen that you can follow the adaptation process of the RW sampler by using

So I wanted to try other samplers (currently the slice) to see if it could ease the process and I was curious to see if there was a similar process during the adapatation phase for the slice samplers (but maybe you would have other suggestions for such cases).

messages.subject: Re: Following adaptation for sampler other than RW
messages.subject_clean: Following adaptation for sampler other than RW
messages.body_plain:
Yes.  Use the method (for example):
conf$setSamplerExecutionOrder( c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) )
or just as well:
conf$setSamplerExecutionOrder( c(1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 4, 1, 5) )

Also, then afterwards, you might find useful:
conf$printSamplers(executionOrder = TRUE)

On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 2:19 PM Rémi Patin <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks a lot for the answer, that helps a lot.
>
> 1. Thank you, I will look into that to test it. Indeed that may be a niche issue to track acceptance without adaptation so I totally understand the choice.
> I always thought that the model kept proposing a new sample until it was accepted before updating the other node so that's a great thing to know it is not the case! Thanks for highlighting the possibility to look into the posterior, I won't use it because I use thinning but that's good to know for the future.
>
> 2. Thanks for pointing me that idea, I will definitely want to try that.
>
> 3. If I understood correctly, at each iteration all nodes are updated but for some of them (56% based on the targeted 0.44 acceptance rate) the value stays the same because the proposal is refused. Is it possible to force more update on one node while other nodes are updated less frequently ? e.g. if node A is highly autocorrelated and have a poor mixing while node B has a good mixing, I would want node A to have a lower acceptance of proposal (therefore less autocorrelated) but to update until one proposal is accepted, before updating node B, so it would spare unneeded calculations on the update of node B, before node A finds a good proposal.
>
> Cheers,
> Rémi
>
>
>
> Le 13/08/2020 à 19:07, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> > To answer your questions:
> >
> > 1. At present, when you specify adaptive=FALSE (thereby using a fixed proposal scale), the RW sampler doesn't record when / how often / the proportion of transitions (the acceptance rate).  And I'm hesitant to slow it down by tracking this, when it's non-adaptive.  That said, you could easily grab the code form GitHub
> > https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/blob/devel/packages/nimble/R/MCMC_samplers.R#L165
> > And modify it so that it still tracks this information even when adaptive=FALSE, but merely doesn't change the scale.  This could be done as easily as removing the one line:
> > scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> > I'll put this modified code, below, and you would only have to remove the RW samplers that are assigned, and add (using conf$addSampler) the new "RW2" sampler, defined below.  To use this sampler, you would need to leave the default of adaptive=TRUE, and also set this nimble system option nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE).
> >
> > Another option would be for you to use the posterior samples calculate the RW acceptance rate, based on the proportion of times it successfully transitions (e.g., the parameter changes value).
> >
> > 2. About the target acceptance rate, right now it's hard-coded into the RW sampler at 0.44.  You can also change this in the code below, if you wish.  Or, if it's useful to you, I'm happy to change this into a (user-modifiable) "control list argument", with default value 0.44.  It would be a straightforward change to make, and could go into our next upcoming release (in a couple weeks).  Let me know if that sounds helpful.
> >
> > Cheers,
> > Daniel
> >
> >
> >
> > sampler_RW2 <- nimbleFunction(
> >     name = 'sampler_RW2',
> >     contains = sampler_BASE,
> >     setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
> >         ## control list extraction
> >         logScale            <- if(!is.null(control$log))                 control$log                 else FALSE
> >         reflective          <- if(!is.null(control$reflective))          control$reflective          else FALSE
> >         adaptive            <- if(!is.null(control$adaptive))            control$adaptive            else TRUE
> >         adaptInterval       <- if(!is.null(control$adaptInterval))       control$adaptInterval       else 200
> >         adaptFactorExponent <- if(!is.null(control$adaptFactorExponent)) control$adaptFactorExponent else 0.8
> >         scale               <- if(!is.null(control$scale))               control$scale               else 1
> >         ## node list generation
> >         targetAsScalar <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
> >         calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
> >         calcNodesNoSelf <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE)
> >         isStochCalcNodesNoSelf <- model$isStoch(calcNodesNoSelf)   ## should be made faster
> >         calcNodesNoSelfDeterm <- calcNodesNoSelf[!isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> >         calcNodesNoSelfStoch <- calcNodesNoSelf[isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> >         ## numeric value generation
> >         scaleOriginal <- scale
> >         timesRan      <- 0
> >         timesAccepted <- 0
> >         timesAdapted  <- 0
> >         scaleHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> >         acceptanceHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> >         if(nimbleOptions('MCMCsaveHistory')) {
> >             saveMCMChistory <- TRUE
> >         } else saveMCMChistory <- FALSE
> >         optimalAR     <- 0.44
> >         gamma1        <- 0
> >         ## checks
> >         if(length(targetAsScalar) > 1)   stop('cannot use RW sampler on more than one target; try RW_block sampler')
> >         if(model$isDiscrete(target))     stop('cannot use RW sampler on discrete-valued target; try slice sampler')
> >         if(logScale & reflective)        stop('cannot use reflective RW sampler on a log scale (i.e. with options log=TRUE and reflective=TRUE')
> >         if(adaptFactorExponent < 0)      stop('cannot use RW sampler with adaptFactorExponent control parameter less than 0')
> >         if(scale < 0)                    stop('cannot use RW sampler with scale control parameter less than 0')
> >     },
> >     run = function() {
> >         currentValue <- model[[target]]
> >         propLogScale <- 0
> >         if(logScale) { propLogScale <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = scale)
> >                        propValue <- currentValue * exp(propLogScale)
> >         } else         propValue <- rnorm(1, mean = currentValue,  sd = scale)
> >         if(reflective) {
> >             lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
> >             upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
> >             while(propValue < lower | propValue > upper) {
> >                 if(propValue < lower) propValue <- 2*lower - propValue
> >                 if(propValue > upper) propValue <- 2*upper - propValue
> >             }
> >         }
> >         model[[target]] <<- propValue
> >         logMHR <- calculateDiff(model, target)
> >         if(logMHR == -Inf) {
> >             nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> >             ## Drawing a random number is needed during first testing
> >             ## of this step in order to keep the random numbers identical
> >             ## to old behavior to see if tests that depend on particular
> >             ## sample sequences pass.  Rather than calling runif(1, 0, 1) here,
> >             ## we call decide() to ensure same behavior.
> >             ## jump <- decide(logMHR)
> >             ## When new behavior is acceptable, we can remove the above line
> >             ## and uncomment the following:
> >             jump <- FALSE
> >         } else {
> >             logMHR <- logMHR + calculateDiff(model, calcNodesNoSelf) + propLogScale
> >             jump <- decide(logMHR)
> >             if(jump) {
> >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> >             } else {
> >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> >             }
> >         }
> >         if(adaptive)     adaptiveProcedure(jump)
> >     },
> >     methods = list(
> >         adaptiveProcedure = function(jump = logical()) {
> >             timesRan <<- timesRan + 1
> >             if(jump)     timesAccepted <<- timesAccepted + 1
> >             if(timesRan %% adaptInterval == 0) {
> >                 acceptanceRate <- timesAccepted / timesRan
> >                 timesAdapted <<- timesAdapted + 1
> >                 if(saveMCMChistory) {
> >                     setSize(scaleHistory, timesAdapted)                 ## scaleHistory
> >                     scaleHistory[timesAdapted] <<- scale                ## scaleHistory
> >                     setSize(acceptanceHistory, timesAdapted)            ## scaleHistory
> >                     acceptanceHistory[timesAdapted] <<- acceptanceRate  ## scaleHistory
> >                 }
> >                 gamma1 <<- 1/((timesAdapted + 3)^adaptFactorExponent)
> >                 gamma2 <- 10 * gamma1
> >                 adaptFactor <- exp(gamma2 * (acceptanceRate - optimalAR))
> >                 ######scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> >                 ## If there are upper and lower bounds, enforce a maximum scale of
> >                 ## 0.5 * (upper-lower).  This is arbitrary but reasonable.
> >                 ## Otherwise, for a poorly-informed posterior,
> >                 ## the scale could grow without bound to try to reduce
> >                 ## acceptance probability.  This creates enormous cost of
> >                 ## reflections.
> >                 if(reflective) {
> >                     lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
> >                     upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
> >                     if(scale >= 0.5*(upper-lower)) {
> >                         scale <<- 0.5*(upper-lower)
> >                     }
> >                 }
> >                 timesRan <<- 0
> >                 timesAccepted <<- 0
> >             }
> >         },
> >         getScaleHistory = function() {       ## scaleHistory
> >             returnType(double(1))
> >             if(saveMCMChistory) {
> >                 return(scaleHistory)
> >             } else {
> >                 print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
> >                 return(numeric(1, 0))
> >             }
> >         },
> >         getAcceptanceHistory = function() {  ## scaleHistory
> >             returnType(double(1))
> >             if(saveMCMChistory) {
> >                 return(acceptanceHistory)
> >             } else {
> >                 print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
> >                 return(numeric(1, 0))
> >             }
> >         },
> >         ##getScaleHistoryExpanded = function() {                                                 ## scaleHistory
> >         ##    scaleHistoryExpanded <- numeric(timesAdapted*adaptInterval, init=FALSE)            ## scaleHistory
> >         ##    for(iTA in 1:timesAdapted)                                                         ## scaleHistory
> >         ##        for(j in 1:adaptInterval)                                                      ## scaleHistory
> >         ##            scaleHistoryExpanded[(iTA-1)*adaptInterval+j] <- scaleHistory[iTA]         ## scaleHistory
> >         ##    returnType(double(1)); return(scaleHistoryExpanded) },                             ## scaleHistory
> >         reset = function() {
> >             scale <<- scaleOriginal
> >             timesRan      <<- 0
> >             timesAccepted <<- 0
> >             timesAdapted  <<- 0
> >             if(saveMCMChistory) {
> >                 scaleHistory  <<- c(0, 0)    ## scaleHistory
> >                 acceptanceHistory  <<- c(0, 0)
> >             }
> >             gamma1 <<- 0
> >         }
> >     )
> > )
> >
> >
> >
> >
> > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 12:56 PM Rémi Patin <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > I meant tracking the history of the acceptance rate of the sampler. Which from what I understood is still meaningful without adaptation for a sampler. Although it may be relatively constant, I would be interested by its level.
> > >
> > > However, I am also interested if you can make the RW sampler to tune itself towards another acceptance rate (right now it tunes toward something like 0.4 if I'm not mistaken)
> > >
> > > Le 13/08/2020 à 18:40, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> > > > Thanks for following up, Rémi.   One question, when you say "would be possible to use non-adaptive RW and still follow acceptance rate?", by the phrase "follow the acceptance rate", do you mean that the RW sampler itself tunes itself towards some "optimal" acceptance rate?  Or, do you mean for you to track (follow) the history of the acceptance rate of the sampler?
> > > >
> > > > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 10:40 AM remi....@gmail.com <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > Hi All,
> > > > > Just a quick follow-up on the different solution I tested following Perry and Daniel advices:
> > > > >
> > > > > - For following the adaptation phase of the slice sampler, I tested the manual solution of stopping the mcmc every 200 runs but it is quite time consuming to run through numerous samplers each time to get the `width` (it is still running in fact). I may test at some point the implementation I proposed in the dev version of nimble, but did not have time for it yet.
> > > > >
> > > > > - I also did some test by fixing the scale of the different RW samplers involved in the problematic nodes. Nothing conclusive for now. But I was wondering if it would be possible to use non-adaptive RW and still follow acceptance rate  ?
> > > > >
> > > > > Best,
> > > > > Rémi
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > On Friday, July 31, 2020 at 5:04:21 PM UTC+2 pdevalpine wrote:
> > > > > > Hi Rémi,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Sure that makes sense.  You could write a for loop to iterate over samplers for many nodes to set the proposal scale and turn the adapt flag FALSE for each one.  I suggested it because it sounded like you were conjecturing that the adaptation has not resulted in proposal scales that you think are most efficient.  (We usually think of efficiency in terms of (effective sample size) / computation time.  The computation time shouldn't change much or at all for different proposal scales, but the effective sample sizes almost certainly will.)  That is possible.  If you increase proposal scale, it may or may not increase effective sample size.  If it does, then fewer iterations would be needed.  I hope that helps.  Let us know if you get interesting results.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > -Perry
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 7:48 AM Rémi PATIN <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > Hi Perry,
> > > > > > > Thank you for the suggestion and the explanations to do it, I will give it a try. I am however a bit afraid to fix the RW proposal scale, because it concerns around ~2000 nodes. So I am not sure whether a single (or even a few) scale for all the nodes could do the trick.
> > > > > > > I suppose if I manually fix the scale to higher value than produced by the adaptation phase, acceptation rate for those nodes will drop leading to slower iteration through those nodes. Meanwhile the samples should be less autocorrelated and less iterations would be needed ?
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Concerning initial values, the model should have relatively good ones for most nodes. I know they have already worked on that and I think that we are currently using older model outputs to initiate the nodes in question. But I will keep that in mind, this could still be problematic.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > > Rémi
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Le vendredi 31 juillet 2020 16:18:06 UTC+2, pdevalpine a écrit :
> > > > > > > > Hi Rémi,
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > If you think the RW proposal scale has adapted to a value that is too small, I can give three suggestions for exploring the issue.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > 1. At the stage of the MCMC configuration (after configureMCMC) but before building the MCMC (before buildMCMC), find the relevant sampler by inspection of mcmcConf$printSamplers() or mcmcConf$getSamplers().  (Here mcmcConf is the object returned by configureMCMC).  Then modify the control list of that sampler to have adapt=FALSE and scale=<your choice>.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > 2. You can make the same settings by modifying the MCMC (after buildMCMC).  If you do it in the uncompiled version (before compileNimble), you can modify mcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$scale and mcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$adapt, where mcmc is the uncompiled MCMC.  Those values will then be copied to the compiled version to initialize it during compileNimble.  If you want to do it after compileNimble (with say Cmcmc instead of mcmc, where Cmcmc is the compiled version), you will need the same nimbleOptions setting Daniel provided.  You may want to do it this way because you could run it for a while, look at the scale value, then manually adjust it and continue running (with reset = FALSE) to experiment.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > 3. Sometimes providing good initial values can improve the outcome of the RW adaptation.  If the initial values are far from the main posterior region, then much of the adaptation can occur during updates that are just finding the main posterior region, which can behave very differently that updates in the main region.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > HTH
> > > > > > > > -Perry
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 6:51 AM Daniel Turek <db...@williams.edu> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > Good question, Rémi.  And I'm glad to hear you found the diagnostic information (scaleHistory, acceptanceRateHistory, etc) in the RW sampler to be helpful.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > At present, there's no such facilities in the slice sampler to record this history of the adaption process.  The slice sampler does adapt (every adaptInterval MCMC iterations), to modify the internal "width" variable, to make this "extension" width of the horizontal slice more suitable for the scale of the posterior distribution.  So, yes, tracking this "widthHistory" would be analogous to the adaptation history information in the RW sampler.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > At present, this information is not tracked in the slice sampler, but similar methods "getWidthHistory" could be added to the slice sampler.  I don't believe there are plans for adding it at the moment, but we would certainly welcome (and review) a pull-request to add this to the system.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Short of that, modifying the sampler code and/or the nimble code base, you could also track this "width history" by extracting the "width" variable from the slice sampler after each MCMC iteration, making sure to set the nimble option:
> > > > > > > > > nimbleOptions(buildInterfacesForCompiledNestedNimbleFunctions = TRUE)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > This would work fine, and accomplish your goals.  A short example showing how to do that is below.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Good luck with this,
> > > > > > > > > Daniel
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > library(nimble)
> > > > > > > > > nimbleOptions(buildInterfacesForCompiledNestedNimbleFunctions = TRUE)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > code <- nimbleCode({
> > > > > > > > >     a ~ dnorm(0, 1)
> > > > > > > > > })
> > > > > > > > > constants <- list()
> > > > > > > > > data <- list()
> > > > > > > > > inits <- list(a = 0)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)
> > > > > > > > > Rmodel$calculate()
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, nodes = NULL)
> > > > > > > > > conf$addSampler('a', 'slice')
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
> > > > > > > > > Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > niter <- 10000
> > > > > > > > > set.seed(0)
> > > > > > > > > widthHistory <- numeric(niter)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > for(i in 1:niter) {
> > > > > > > > >     Cmcmc$run(1, reset = (i==1))
> > > > > > > > >     widthHistory[i] <- Cmcmc$samplerFunctions[[1]]$width
> > > > > > > > > }
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > samples <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > plot(1:niter, widthHistory, type = 'l')
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 2:27 AM Rémi PATIN <remi...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > Hi all,
> > > > > > > > > > I have seen that you can follow the adaptation process of the RW sampler by using
> > > > > > > > > > cmcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$getScaleHistory()
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > and
> > > > > > > > > > cmcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$getAcceptanceHistory()
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > I suppose it is not yet possible (but maybe scheduled at some point?) to get similar information for other samplers such as slice for instance ?
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > I have some nodes for which the RW adaptation decreases greatly the scale to keep acceptance rate high enough, which produces some highly autocorrelated samples. So I wanted to try other samplers (currently the slice) to see if it could ease the process and I was curious to see if there was a similar process during the adapatation phase for the slice samplers (but maybe you would have other suggestions for such cases).
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > Thanks in advance,
> > > > > > > > > > Rémi

> > Le 13/08/2020 à 19:07, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> > > To answer your questions:
> > >
> > > 1. At present, when you specify adaptive=FALSE (thereby using a fixed proposal scale), the RW sampler doesn't record when / how often / the proportion of transitions (the acceptance rate).  And I'm hesitant to slow it down by tracking this, when it's non-adaptive.  That said, you could easily grab the code form GitHub
> > > https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/blob/devel/packages/nimble/R/MCMC_samplers.R#L165
> > > And modify it so that it still tracks this information even when adaptive=FALSE, but merely doesn't change the scale.  This could be done as easily as removing the one line:
> > > scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> > > I'll put this modified code, below, and you would only have to remove the RW samplers that are assigned, and add (using conf$addSampler) the new "RW2" sampler, defined below.  To use this sampler, you would need to leave the default of adaptive=TRUE, and also set this nimble system option nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE).
> > >
> > > Another option would be for you to use the posterior samples calculate the RW acceptance rate, based on the proportion of times it successfully transitions (e.g., the parameter changes value).
> > >
> > > 2. About the target acceptance rate, right now it's hard-coded into the RW sampler at 0.44.  You can also change this in the code below, if you wish.  Or, if it's useful to you, I'm happy to change this into a (user-modifiable) "control list argument", with default value 0.44.  It would be a straightforward change to make, and could go into our next upcoming release (in a couple weeks).  Let me know if that sounds helpful.
> > >
> > > Cheers,
> > > Daniel
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > sampler_RW2 <- nimbleFunction(
> > >     name = 'sampler_RW2',
> > >     contains = sampler_BASE,
> > >     setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
> > >         ## control list extraction
> > >         logScale            <- if(!is.null(control$log))                 control$log                 else FALSE
> > >         reflective          <- if(!is.null(control$reflective))          control$reflective          else FALSE
> > >         adaptive            <- if(!is.null(control$adaptive))            control$adaptive            else TRUE
> > >         adaptInterval       <- if(!is.null(control$adaptInterval))       control$adaptInterval       else 200
> > >         adaptFactorExponent <- if(!is.null(control$adaptFactorExponent)) control$adaptFactorExponent else 0.8
> > >         scale               <- if(!is.null(control$scale))               control$scale               else 1
> > >         ## node list generation
> > >         targetAsScalar <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
> > >         calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
> > >         calcNodesNoSelf <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE)
> > >         isStochCalcNodesNoSelf <- model$isStoch(calcNodesNoSelf)   ## should be made faster
> > >         calcNodesNoSelfDeterm <- calcNodesNoSelf[!isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> > >         calcNodesNoSelfStoch <- calcNodesNoSelf[isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> > >         ## numeric value generation
> > >         scaleOriginal <- scale
> > >         timesRan      <- 0
> > >         timesAccepted <- 0
> > >         timesAdapted  <- 0
> > >         scaleHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> > >         acceptanceHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> > >         if(nimbleOptions('MCMCsaveHistory')) {
> > >             saveMCMChistory <- TRUE
> > >         } else saveMCMChistory <- FALSE
> > >         optimalAR     <- 0.44
> > >         gamma1        <- 0
> > >         ## checks
> > >         if(length(targetAsScalar) > 1)   stop('cannot use RW sampler on more than one target; try RW_block sampler')
> > >         if(model$isDiscrete(target))     stop('cannot use RW sampler on discrete-valued target; try slice sampler')
> > >         if(logScale & reflective)        stop('cannot use reflective RW sampler on a log scale (i.e. with options log=TRUE and reflective=TRUE')
> > >         if(adaptFactorExponent < 0)      stop('cannot use RW sampler with adaptFactorExponent control parameter less than 0')
> > >         if(scale < 0)                    stop('cannot use RW sampler with scale control parameter less than 0')
> > >     },
> > >     run = function() {
> > >         currentValue <- model[[target]]
> > >         propLogScale <- 0
> > >         if(logScale) { propLogScale <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = scale)
> > >                        propValue <- currentValue * exp(propLogScale)
> > >         } else         propValue <- rnorm(1, mean = currentValue,  sd = scale)
> > >         if(reflective) {
> > >             lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
> > >             upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
> > >             while(propValue < lower | propValue > upper) {
> > >                 if(propValue < lower) propValue <- 2*lower - propValue
> > >                 if(propValue > upper) propValue <- 2*upper - propValue
> > >             }
> > >         }
> > >         model[[target]] <<- propValue
> > >         logMHR <- calculateDiff(model, target)
> > >         if(logMHR == -Inf) {
> > >             nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > >             ## Drawing a random number is needed during first testing
> > >             ## of this step in order to keep the random numbers identical
> > >             ## to old behavior to see if tests that depend on particular
> > >             ## sample sequences pass.  Rather than calling runif(1, 0, 1) here,
> > >             ## we call decide() to ensure same behavior.
> > >             ## jump <- decide(logMHR)
> > >             ## When new behavior is acceptable, we can remove the above line
> > >             ## and uncomment the following:
> > >             jump <- FALSE
> > >         } else {
> > >             logMHR <- logMHR + calculateDiff(model, calcNodesNoSelf) + propLogScale
> > >             jump <- decide(logMHR)
> > >             if(jump) {
> > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> > >             } else {
> > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> > >             }
> > >         }
> > >         if(adaptive)     adaptiveProcedure(jump)
> > >     },
> > >     methods = list(
> > >         adaptiveProcedure = function(jump = logical()) {
> > >             timesRan <<- timesRan + 1
> > >             if(jump)     timesAccepted <<- timesAccepted + 1
> > >             if(timesRan %% adaptInterval == 0) {
> > >                 acceptanceRate <- timesAccepted / timesRan
> > >                 timesAdapted <<- timesAdapted + 1
> > >                 if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > >                     setSize(scaleHistory, timesAdapted)                 ## scaleHistory
> > >                     scaleHistory[timesAdapted] <<- scale                ## scaleHistory
> > >                     setSize(acceptanceHistory, timesAdapted)            ## scaleHistory
> > >                     acceptanceHistory[timesAdapted] <<- acceptanceRate  ## scaleHistory
> > >                 }
> > >                 gamma1 <<- 1/((timesAdapted + 3)^adaptFactorExponent)
> > >                 gamma2 <- 10 * gamma1
> > >                 adaptFactor <- exp(gamma2 * (acceptanceRate - optimalAR))
> > >                 ######scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> > >                 ## If there are upper and lower bounds, enforce a maximum scale of
> > >                 ## 0.5 * (upper-lower).  This is arbitrary but reasonable.
> > >                 ## Otherwise, for a poorly-informed posterior,
> > >                 ## the scale could grow without bound to try to reduce
> > >                 ## acceptance probability.  This creates enormous cost of
> > >                 ## reflections.
> > >                 if(reflective) {
> > >                     lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
> > >                     upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
> > >                     if(scale >= 0.5*(upper-lower)) {
> > >                         scale <<- 0.5*(upper-lower)
> > >                     }
> > >                 }
> > >                 timesRan <<- 0
> > >                 timesAccepted <<- 0
> > >             }
> > >         },
> > >         getScaleHistory = function() {       ## scaleHistory
> > >             returnType(double(1))

> > >         }

messages.body_plain:
I'm getting negative values in my posterior samples even though my custom-written sampler is strictly positive. Something is obviously wrong.

The Jeffreys' prior for parameter b ~ sd(1/(b+S)) where sd() is standard deviation and S is a vector of data.

I've been tinkering with my custom distribution 'db' and so I first call:
deregisterDistributions('db')

Since my distribution is a function of data, I just stick those data into the density function as 'Si':

deregisterDistributions('db')
    #BEGIN density function for beta, b
    db<- nimbleFunction(
      run = function(x = double(0), log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
        Si =  c(1978,  2477,  2119, 13707, 13129,  3360,  1995,  8774,  2429,  4906, 16811, 15000, 19250,  1686,  4706, 20550, 1361,  7102)
        returnType(double(0))
        logProb <- log(sd(1/(x+Si)))
        if(log) return(logProb)
        else return(exp(logProb))
      })

I use rejection sampling for the random sampler.  This sure looks like 'b' is strictly positive:
rb<- nimbleFunction(
      run = function(n = integer(0)){
        Si =  c(1978,  2477,  2119, 13707, 13129,  3360,  1995,  8774,  2429,  4906, 16811, 15000, 19250,  1686,  4706, 20550, 1361,  7102)

        returnType(double(0))
        if(n != 1) print("rb only allows n = 1; using n = 1.")
        x<-runif(1,0,10000)
        b<-runif(1,0,0.0003)
        while (b > sd(1/(x+Si))){

messages.body_plain:
hi Matt,

The 'r' function in a user-defined distribution (or any of the distributions we provide) is NOT used in MCMC sampling (except for the case of a node that has no dependent nodes). Rather, NIMBLE's configureMCMC function assigns samplers to each node. If you use the "printSamplers" method on an MCMC configuration object you can see what samplers are being assigned to the different nodes in the model.  And if your density function is positive for negative values of the random variable, then our samplers will sample negative values during the MCMC.

Another way to put this is that in NIMBLE, the "r" function would sample from the prior, but in MCMC sampling one needs to sample from the posterior (conditional on the current values of the other nodes in the model).

If you would like to set up a specific sampler that will get used in an MCMC, you'll need to write a user-defined sampler, as discussed in Section 15.5 of the NIMBLE User Manual.

-Chris

hi Matt,

Ok, glad that some of the issue was just a question of language.

NIMBLE's MCMC uses the "d" function to calculate priors (and likelihoods), so the key is whether the "d" function implements the fact that your prior is strictly positive by assigning 0 density to negative values of the random variable. The "r" function is unused unless a specific algorithm needs to simulate from the prior, which in our built-in MCMC samplers only happens for "predictive" nodes, i.e., those with no dependents.

-chris

> > > > Yes.  compileNimble writes C++ code, compiles it, and links it to a  static library that comes with nimble, each result in files.  Also there is a once-per-session compilation step, which is why the first call to compileNimble is always slower than subsequent calls.  The files are normally placed in tempdir(), the temporary directory automatically created by R for each session that is available for use by packages (or the user) and cleaned up upon R exit (usually).  One option would be for you to iterate through your models such that you invoke a new R session for each model.  For example, you could have a primary R session (or other script) that uses system2 to call Rscript to run one case.  That would create separate R process for each case, which should clean up its own tempdir() upon exit.   Another option would be to control where nimble puts its files by using the dirName argument to compileNimble and then adding a step in your code that removes files (curiously named unlink() in R) from wherever you put them. If you use that option, you might also want to use nimble:::clearCompiled(obj) after each case, where obj is any object associated with one nimble project, such as the model. In your model, you specify your spatio-temporal variation using distributions placed on the time series innovations (the phi_sp). This leads to an explosion in the dependencies for the latent process values when the MCMC is being set up and being sampled, which leads to large memory usage and slow sampling. A simple example of this is discussed in materials from our June workshop - see https://github.com/nimble-training/nimble-virtual-2020 in the content/4_improving_mcmc  module under "Think like a graph: reducing dependencies".
> > >
> > > Unfortunately the solution posed in that material, which is to 'center' the process at time t on the process at time t-1, won't work with a CAR model because we haven't set up the CAR model to take a vector mean.
> > > An alternative to a CAR structure would be to use a Gaussian process or a spline, which do allow for such centering. We have some details on Gaussian processes and splines, again in our June workshop, in content/7_spatial_models.  The basic idea would be to have something like this as your time-evolving process (I'm omitting the scaling you have with eta and sigma_phi as I just want to illustrate the basic idea):
> > >
> > > phi_full[1:s, m, i] ~ dmvnorm(phi_full[1:s, m-1, i], cov = C[1:s, 1:s])
> > >
> > > where you'd have to set up "C" as a spatial covariance matrix. Alternatively, you could set up splines to capture the spatial variation and have the spline coefficients evolve over time.
> > >
> > > In general, getting good MCMC performance for a large spatio-temporal problem like this can be hard. This will particularly be the case if the number of spatial locations, 's', gets into the thousands.
> > >
> > > -chris

Hmm, odd. That looks like a filesystem problem, which might not be
related to nimble.

1) Before running compileNimble, you could try making sure the
expected R tempdir exists. To find the R tempdir, do "tempdir()".
Then see if this directory exists (but where you replace XYZ based on
what you see from tempdir():

C:\Users\abl6\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpXYZ

If it exists, see if it is possible to create files or directories
within it, which is what NIMBLE needs to be able to do.

2) You could also try using the dirName argument to compileNimble to
be a filesystem location where you know you have permission to create
files.

-chris

messages.subject: Multi-species, single-season occupancy model: error in quantile.default
messages.subject_clean: Multi-species, single-season occupancy model: error in quantile.default
messages.body_plain:
Good morning everyone,

My colleague, Michelle Pretorius <https://groups.google.com/g/nimble-users/c/ZZIn3gzKKuY/m/Rws9HnvyBQAJ>, recently introduced me to nimble, and like her I am eager to explore its applications (previously I have used STAN to run my multi-spp occu models). Following in her footsteps, we have been trying to run a multi-species, single season occupancy model from Ponisio et al. 2020 <https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ece3.6053>, whilst adding in parameters to estimate species richness, similar to Zipkin et al. 2010 <https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0006320709004819?via%3Dihub>. To do so we are utilising camera trapping data from 3 sites, namely A, B and C. The data does exhibit overdispersion, and I have posted the full code below.

However, while running the model we have been getting a fatal error:
|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|
|-------------------------------------------------------|
Error in quantile.default(x, 0.025) :
  missing values and NaN's not allowed if 'na.rm' is FALSE
​
We suspect that this error is a result of poor model initialization, yet unfortunately we are unsure as to how to troubleshoot this. We have amended the code to not skip over NA records within the input count data in the observation model, as Andrew previously suggested <https://groups.google.com/g/nimble-users/c/LFEQ4sBUItY>, however this does not appear to have had any impact. In addition, we have noticed that using the direct run() function as opposed to runMCMC() appears to negate this error- but are struggling to understand why. As I understand it, runMCMC allows one to specifiy more arguments and it extracts the samples for you, whilst run() does not. Again, I believe this points to bad model initialisation.

In addition, we get multiple warnings. We unsderstand that these can be overlooked:
warning: problem initializing stochastic node Z[10, 57]: logProb is -Inf.
warning: problem initializing stochastic node Z[12, 57]: logProb is -Inf.
... etc...

warning: problem initializing stochastic node X[409, 6, 18]: logProb is -Inf.
warning: problem initializing stochastic node X[409, 10, 18]: logProb is -Inf.
... etc...
​
Any assistance/suggestions would be greatly appreciated.
Regards,
Zoe Woodgate
###########################################################################################
# INTIAL DATA PREP
###########################################################################################

# Load data
survey.data <- read_delim("obs_dates.csv", delim = ",")
survey.dates <- read_delim("point_dates.csv", delim = ",")
survey.cov <- read_delim( "habitat.csv", delim = ";")

# remove duplicate rows in dates column
# based on point column
survey.dates  <- survey.dates [!duplicated(survey.dates $point), ]

# add in random species that covers the stations with zero detections
# 12 stations had zero detections
point <- c(145, 154, 156, 161, 174, 190, 193, 194, 202, 203, 229, 273)
date <- rep(NA, 12)
time <- rep(NA, 12)
species <- rep("random", 12)
individuals <- rep(1,12)
repetition <- c(11, 10, 10, 11, 11, 11, 10, 10, 10, 10, 11, 11)

# Make new data frame for these missing stations/points
missing.data <- data.frame(point, date, time, species, individuals, repetition)

#Now add them to original data file
survey.data <- rbind(survey.data,missing.data)

sort(unique(survey.data$species))
# random species is "species 36"

###########################################################################################
# HISTORIES (following Ponisio et al. 2020)
###########################################################################################

# Use function to create multiple histories for each species per site
histories <- createEncounterHistory(survey.data)
histories <- addMissingData(histories, survey.dates)

histories$X <- histories$X[,,-36] #remove random species

# Check random species is removed
dim.names <- dimnames(histories$X)

X <- histories$X

# nzeroes is the number of all zero encounter histories to be added
# Augments the original dataset
n.zeroes = 10

X.aug <- zeroAugment(histories, n.zeroes)

###########################################################################################
# PREP DATA FOR MODEL
###########################################################################################

# Pull out the number of unique points, species and # reps per station
num.species <- length(unique(dim.names[[3]]))
num.points <- length(unique(survey.data$point))
num.reps <- apply(survey.dates[,-(1:1)],
                  1,
                  function(x) length(which(!is.na <http://is.na>(x))))

# Create a vector to indicate which 'site' (called habitat for ease) type each point is in
# For each site, each camera =1, then other site = 0
# Repeat for all three sites
N <- rep(0, 451)
A.id <- c(rep(1, 119), rep(0, (451-119)))
B.id <- c(rep(0, 119), rep(1, 176), rep(0, (451-(119+176))))
C.id <- c(rep(0, 295), rep(1, (451-295)))

## Standardize variables
mpr <- as.numeric(factor(survey.cov$mpr))

tri <-  siteLevelStandardized(survey.cov$tri)
tri.linear <- tri$linear

msavi <- siteLevelStandardized(survey.cov$msavi)
msavi.linear <- msavi$linear

trail <- siteLevelStandardized(survey.cov$trail)
trail <- trail$linear

date <- surveyLevelStandardized(survey.dates[,-(1:1)])
date.linear <- date$linear

# NA's -> 0's
date.linear[is.na <http://is.na>(date.linear)] <- 0

# Z data for whether or not a species was ever observed
# zs with 1s as 1s and 0s as NAs
class(X.aug)
zs <- apply(X.aug, c(1, 3), max, na.rm=TRUE)
zs[zs == 0] <- NA
zs[!is.finite(zs)] <- NA

model.data <- list(Z = zs,
                   X = X.aug,
                   mpr=mpr,
                   A.id=A.id,
                   B.id=B.id,
                   C.id=C.id,
                   tri.linear=tri.linear,
                   msavi.linear=msavi.linear,
                   trail=trail,
                   date.linear = date.linear)

psi.mean.draw <- runif(1, 0.25, 1)

# initial values

omega.draw <- runif(1, num.species/(num.species + n.zeroes), 1)

# initial conditions. 1 should be NA, NA should be a 0 or 1
zinits <- zs
zinits[zinits == 1] <- 2
zinits[is.na <http://is.na>(zinits)] <- sample(0:1, sum(is.na <http://is.na>(zinits)),
                                replace=TRUE)
zinits[zinits == 2] <- NA

# Make list of intial value data for model to call upon

initsList <-list(Z=zinits,
                 omega = omega.draw,
                 w = c(rep(1, num.species),
                       rbinom(n.zeroes, size = 1, prob = omega.draw)),
                 u.A = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 v.A = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 u.B = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes) ,
                 v.B = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 u.C = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes) ,
                 v.C = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 a1 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 a2 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 a3 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 b1 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes),
                 b2 = rnorm(num.species + n.zeroes))

# Further information needed for the model
constants <- list(num.species = num.species,
                  num.points = num.points,
                  num.reps = num.reps,
                  n.zeroes = n.zeroes)

################################################################################
# BUGS CODE WITH NIMBLE
################################################################################

# Construct the initial values
ms.ss.occ <- nimbleCode({
  ## Define prior distributions for community-level model parameters

  omega ~ dunif(0,1)

  A.occ.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.uA <- log(A.occ.mean) - log(1-A.occ.mean)
  sigma.uA ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.uA <-  1/(sigma.uA*sigma.uA)

  B.occ.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.uB <- log(B.occ.mean) - log(1-B.occ.mean)
  sigma.uB ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.uB <-  1/(sigma.uB*sigma.uB)

  C.occ.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.uC <- log(C.occ.mean) - log(1-C.occ.mean)
  sigma.uC ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.uC <-  1/(sigma.uC*sigma.uC)

  A.det.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.vA <- log(A.det.mean) - log(1-A.det.mean)
  sigma.vA ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.vA <-  1/(sigma.vA*sigma.vA)

  B.det.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.vB <- log(B.det.mean) - log(1-B.det.mean)
  sigma.vB ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.vB <-  1/(sigma.vB*sigma.vB)

  C.det.mean ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu.vC <- log(C.det.mean) - log(1-C.det.mean)
  sigma.vC ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.vC <-  1/(sigma.vC*sigma.vC)

  ## random effects
  mu.a1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.a1 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.a1 <-  1/(sigma.a1*sigma.a1)

  mu.a2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.a2 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.a2 <-  1/(sigma.a2*sigma.a2)

  mu.a3 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.a3 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.a3 <-  1/(sigma.a3*sigma.a3)

  mu.b1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.b1 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.b1 <-  1/(sigma.b1*sigma.b1)

  mu.b2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.001)
  sigma.b2 ~ dunif(0, 100)
  tau.b2 <-  1/(sigma.b2*sigma.b2)

  for (i in 1:(num.species + n.zeroes)) {
    ## Create priors for species i from the community level prior distributions

    w[i] ~ dbern(omega)

    u.A[i] ~ dnorm(mu.uA, tau.uA)
    u.B[i] ~ dnorm(mu.uB, tau.uB)
    u.C[i] ~ dnorm(mu.uC, tau.uC)

    a1[i] ~ dnorm(mu.a1, tau.a1)
    a2[i] ~ dnorm(mu.a2, tau.a2)
    a3[i] ~ dnorm(mu.a3, tau.a3)

    v.A[i] ~ dnorm(mu.vA, tau.vA)
    v.B[i] ~ dnorm(mu.vB, tau.vB)
    v.C[i] ~ dnorm(mu.vC, tau.vC)

    b1[i] ~ dnorm(mu.b1, tau.b1)
    b2[i] ~ dnorm(mu.b2, tau.b2)

    ## Create a loop to estimate the Z matrix (true occurrence for species i at point j).

    ## A=2; B=1; C=0

    for (j in 1:num.points) {
      logit(psi[j,i]) <- u.A[i]*A.id[j] +
        u.B[i]*B.id[j] +
        u.C[i]*C.id[j] +
        a1[i]*mpr[j] +
        a2[i]*tri.linear[j] +
        a3[i]*msavi.linear[j]

      mu.psi[j,i] <- psi[j,i]*w[i]
      Z[j,i] ~ dbern(mu.psi[j,i])

      ## Create a loop to estimate detection for species i at point k during sampling period k.

      for (k in 1:max(num.reps[j])) {
        logit(p[j,k,i]) <-  v.A[i]*A.id[j] +
          v.B[i]*B.id[j] +
          v.C[i]*C.id[j] +
          b1[i]*trail[j]+

), MCMCmonitorAllSampledNodes=TRUE)

# Specify which nodes the model needs to call

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

After accounting for spatial autocorrelation in various community N-mixture models estimated, I am currently using runCrossValidate( ) to conduct k-fold cross-validation to select between candidate models. As Hooten and Hobbs (2015) note, WAIC is not recommended for use in model selection when considering models that incorporate correlated error structures (e.g., spatial [conditional autoregressive] terms); hence, I am using cross-validation with a loss function, instead.

With the help of the user manual, I incorporated a loss function (i.e. RMSE) into runCrossValidate( ):
{
# Define the fold function
commNmix_FoldFunction <- function(i) {
  foldNodes_i <- paste0('Yc[', i, ', , ]')  # Will return 'Yc[1 , , ]' for i = 1 (e.g., based on nsite)
  return(foldNodes_i)
}

# Define the loss function
RMSE_lossFunction <- function(simulatedDataValues, actualDataValues) {
  dataLength <- length(simulatedDataValues) # simulatedDataValues is a vector
  SSE <- 0

  for(i in 1:dataLength){
    SSE <- SSE + (simulatedDataValues[i] - actualDataValues[i])^2
  }

  MSE <- SSE / dataLength
  RMSE <- sqrt(MSE)
  return(RMSE)
}

commNmix_MCMCconfiguration <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)

crossValOutput <- runCrossValidate(MCMCconfiguration = commNmix_MCMCconfiguration,
                                   k = 5, nBootReps = 1000,
                                   foldFunction = commNmix_FoldFunction,
                                   lossFunction = RMSE_lossFunction,
                                   MCMCcontrol = list(niter = 12500,
                                                      nburnin = 2500))
}

After successful compilation, runCrossValidate( ) returns the following:
{
> crossValOutput
$CVvalue
[1] 5.506311

$CVstandardError
[1] 0

$foldCVinfo
$foldCVinfo[[1]]
        foldCVvalue foldCVstandardError
           6.927172            0.000000

$foldCVinfo[[2]]
        foldCVvalue foldCVstandardError
            6.85878             0.00000

$foldCVinfo[[3]]
        foldCVvalue foldCVstandardError
           4.967034            0.000000

$foldCVinfo[[4]]
        foldCVvalue foldCVstandardError
           4.464143            0.000000

$foldCVinfo[[5]]
        foldCVvalue foldCVstandardError
           4.314428            0.000000
}

I am curious as to how/why the CV standard errors are each estimated to be 0. Could this be related to (a) my use of cross-validation on a community N-mixture model, (b) missing information in my fold/loss function(s), (c) a bug in the source code for runCrossValidate( ), or (d) something else?

Perhaps the standard errors are precisely 0, but that's suspicious to me. Thank you for your suggestions in advance!

Best,
Andrew

Hi Zoe,

Thanks for your message.

Let me give a quick answer by pointing you towards some similar issues that have come up on the list:

https://groups.google.com/u/3/g/nimble-users/c/ZZIn3gzKKuY

https://groups.google.com/u/3/g/nimble-users/c/9PmFGuJCrbg

Those illustrate how you can use the model object to inspect variables, log probabilities of stochastic nodes, and control calculations to isolate where something may not be fully initialized.

I am thinking it may be helpful for us to put some easy-to-find guidance up on how to inspect model objects to track down issues like this, maybe as a new example on the web site.  My impression is that perhaps users jumping over from other tools aren't easily seeing what can be done, but let me know how others see it.

Good luck and please let us know if those pointers aren't enough to get you going.

-Perry
